extracted.subtask_description: Form paragraphs and examiner guidance for rejecting or evaluating patent claims under 35 U.S.C. 112 (second, fourth, and sixth paragraphs) — indefiniteness, means-plus-function, omitted elements/steps, dependent claim form, and related examiner responses to applicant arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to Claim Inventor’s Invention (35 U.S.C. 112(b), pre-AIA 112, 2nd para)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as failing to set forth the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the applicant(s) regard as their invention. Evidence that claim [2] fail(s) to correspond in scope with that which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the applicant(s) regard as the invention can be found in the reply filed [3]. In that paper, the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the applicant has stated [4], and this statement indicates that the invention is different from what is defined in the claim(s) because [5].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. Use only where inventor/applicant has stated, somewhere other than in the application as filed, that the invention is different from what is defined in the claims. In bracket 3 identify the submission and date; in bracket 4 set forth what was stated; in bracket 5 explain how statement indicates a different invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Particularly Point Out and Distinctly Claim (Indefinite) (35 U.S.C.112(b), pre-AIA 112, 2nd para)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor, or for pre-AIA the applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103. Follow with one or more of form paragraphs 7.34.02–7.34.11 as applicable; if none appropriate supply a full explanation of claim deficiency. Whenever possible, identify particular term(s)/limitation(s) rendering the claim indefinite and state why. If the scope can be determined by one of ordinary skill, this rejection is inappropriate. See MPEP §§2171–2174. For pro se applicants see 7.34.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology Used Inconsistent with Accepted Meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant acts as his or her own lexicographer to specifically define a term of a claim contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the claim term and set forth the uncommon definition so as to put one reasonably skilled in the art on notice that the applicant intended to so redefine that claim term. The term “[1]” in claim [2] is used by the claim to mean “[3],” while the accepted meaning is “[4].” The term is indefinite because the specification does not clearly redefine the claim term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 3 point out the meaning assigned by applicant's claims (considering entire disclosure). In bracket 4 point out accepted meaning with support (textbook/dictionary). Must be preceded by 7.34.01. Use only where specification does not clearly redefine the term. See MPEP §2173.05(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Term — Term of Degree Rendering Claim Indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: The term “[1]” in claim [2] is a relative term which renders the claim indefinite. The term “[1]” is not defined by the claim, the specification does not provide a standard for ascertaining the requisite degree, and one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of the scope of the invention. [3]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 3 explain which parameter, quantity, or other limitation is rendered indefinite by the term in bracket 1. Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Range/Limitation And Narrow Range/Limitation in Same Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range or limitation together with a narrow range or limitation that falls within the broad range or limitation (in the same claim) is considered indefinite, since the resulting claim does not clearly set forth the metes and bounds of the patent protection desired. Example: claim [1] recites the broad recitation [2] and also recites [3] which is the narrower statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain broader (bracket 2) and narrower (bracket 3) ranges and locations in claim. May be modified to fit other indefiniteness instances. Must be preceded by 7.34.01. See MPEP §2173.05(c) and cited Board decisions (Ex parte Wu, Steigewald, Hall, Hasche).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of Antecedent Basis in the Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] recites the limitation [2] in [3]. There is insufficient antecedent basis for this limitation in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert limitation that lacks antecedent basis (e.g., 'said lever'). In bracket 3 identify where in claim the limitation appears. Use ONLY in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes scope indeterminate. Must be preceded by 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Claims (claiming a use without steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provides for the use of [2], but, since the claim does not set forth any steps involved in the method/process, it is unclear what method/process applicant is intending to encompass. A claim is indefinite where it merely recites a use without any active, positive steps delimiting how this use is actually practiced. Claim [3] is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because the claimed recitation of a use, without setting forth any steps involved in the process, results in an improper definition of a process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Dunki and Clinical Products, Ltd. v. Brenner for examples. Use when a claim defines 'use' but lacks steps making it a proper process claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'For Example'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'for example' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitation(s) following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01. See MPEP §2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Or the Like'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'or the like' renders the claim(s) indefinite because the claim(s) include(s) elements not actually disclosed (those encompassed by 'or the like'), thereby rendering the scope of the claim(s) unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.34.01. See MPEP §2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite Claim Language: 'Such As'
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding claim [1], the phrase 'such as' renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.34.01. See MPEP §2173.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifier of 'Means' Lacks Function
rubrics_metrics.description: (¶ 7.34.11) Examiner Note: In bracket 2, insert what is being used. For example: the monoclonal antibodies of claim 4, where the claim recites 'a method for using monoclonal antibodies of claim 4 to purify interferon.' See MPEP §2173.05(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by 7.34.01. Use when words preceding 'means' or substitute do not convey function vs. structure; see guidance on invoking 35 U.S.C. 112(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Are a Literal Translation (narrative, indefinite, foreign-language translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] uses 'means' or a generic placeholder and is preceded by the word(s) '[2]'. It is unclear whether these words convey function or structure. The claims are generally narrative and indefinite, failing to conform with current U.S. practice. They appear to be a literal translation into English from a foreign document and are replete with grammatical and idiomatic errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when it cannot be determined from the specification whether words convey function or structure; must be preceded by 7.34.01. If claim element recites structure for performing the function, 112(f) will not be invoked. See Ex parte Klumb and MPEP §2173.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Steps Omitted (omitting essential process steps) (35 U.S.C.112(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being incomplete for omitting essential steps, such omission amounting to a gap between the steps. The omitted steps are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2 recite omitted steps and give rationale for considering them critical or essential. See MPEP §2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Elements Omitted (omitting essential structural elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being incomplete for omitting essential elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the elements. The omitted elements are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2 recite omitted elements and explain why they are critical/essential. See MPEP §2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Cooperative Relationships Omitted (omitting structural cooperative relationships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as being incomplete for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the necessary structural connections. The omitted structural cooperative relationships are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be preceded by 7.30.02 or 7.103. In bracket 2 recite omitted structural cooperative relationships and give rationale for considering them critical/essential. See MPEP §2172.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection Under 35 U.S.C.112, Pro Se (claims drafted by pro se applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as failing to define the invention in the manner required by 35 U.S.C. 112(b). The claim(s) are narrative in form and replete with indefinite language. The structure which goes to make up the device must be clearly and positively specified and organized to present a complete operative device. The claim(s) must be in one sentence form only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for pro se applicants; note claim format examples in cited patents. This paragraph addresses common pro se drafting deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear Whether Recited Structure/Material/Acts Preclude Application of 35 U.S.C.112(f) (¶7.34.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim limitation '[1]' uses the phrase 'means for' or 'step for' or a generic placeholder coupled with functional language, but it is modified by some structure, material, or acts recited in the claim. It is unclear whether the recited structure, material, or acts are sufficient for performing the claimed function because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may amend the claim to avoid invoking 112(f) or show that the phrase is functional without sufficient structure, or amend to add structure. In bracket 1 recite limitation; in bracket 2 explain why unclear. This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Asserts Claim Limitation Invokes 112(f) but 'Means for' Not Used (¶7.34.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant asserts that the claim element '[1]' invokes 35 U.S.C. 112(f) even though the phrase 'means for' is not used. However, it is unclear whether the claim element invokes 112(f) because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may (a) amend to include 'means for' modified by functional language and not by sufficient structure, (b) amend so it will not be interpreted under 112(f), or (c) amend the written description to expressly recite corresponding structure/material/acts without new matter. Alternatively applicant may present sufficient showing that the written description implicitly discloses the corresponding structure. In brackets: 1 recite limitation; 2 explain why unclear. Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01. See MPEP §707.07(a) and §2181.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Disclosure or Insufficient Disclosure of Corresponding Structure/Material/Acts for Function (¶7.34.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim element '[1]' invokes 35 U.S.C. 112(f). However, the written description fails to disclose the corresponding structure, material, or acts for the claimed function. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 recite limitation invoking 112(f). In bracket 2 explain why disclosure is insufficient. Applicant may state on record what corresponding structure/material/acts implicitly set forth (see 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP §§608.01(o), 2181). Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fails To Clearly Link/Associate Disclosed Structure/Material/Acts to Function (¶7.34.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim element '[1]' invokes 35 U.S.C. 112(f). However, the written description fails to clearly link or associate the disclosed structure, material, or acts to the claimed function such that one of ordinary skill in the art would recognize what structure, material, or acts perform the claimed function. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may (a) amend the claim to avoid 112(f), (b) amend the specification to clearly link structure/material/acts to the function without new matter, or (c) state on record where in the specification the corresponding structure/material/acts are set forth and linked to the function (see 37 CFR 1.175(d) and MPEP §§608.01(o), 2181). Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification Objected; Written Description Only Implicitly/Inherently Discloses Structure (¶7.34.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim element '[1]' invokes 35 U.S.C. 112(f). The written description only implicitly or inherently sets forth the corresponding structure, material, or acts that perform the claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP §§608.01(o), 2181 applicant should (a) amend claim to avoid 112(f), (b) amend written description to expressly recite corresponding structure/material/acts and clearly link to function without new matter, or (c) state on record what corresponding structure/material/acts implicitly or inherently set forth in the specification perform the claimed function. In bracket 1 recite limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Limitation Interpreted under 35 U.S.C.112(f) (¶7.34.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim limitation(s) '[1]' has/have been interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) because it uses a generic placeholder '[2]' coupled with functional language '[3]' without reciting sufficient [structure/material/acts]. A review of the specification shows the following appears to be the corresponding structure described: [6].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant disputes interpretation, they must identify corresponding structure with reference to specification page/line and drawing reference characters in response. If applicant does not intend invocation of 112(f), they may amend or present showing that claim recites sufficient structure. Use only when additional explanation regarding treatment under 112(f) is necessary. May be used for multiple claims. Provide bracketed items 1–6 as instructed. See MPEP §2173 and 2011 Supplementary Examination Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant Asserts Claim Limitation Does Not Invoke 112(f) but No Structure is Recited (¶7.34.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant asserts that claim element '[1]' does not invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f). However, it is unclear whether the element invokes 112(f) because [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may (a) amend the claim to add sufficient structure/material/acts to perform the function, or (b) present sufficient showing that the claim limitation recites sufficient structure/material/acts to preclude application of 112(f). See MPEP §2181. Use when applicant replies asserting no invocation of 112(f) though no structure is provided. Must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or Trade Name as a Limitation in the Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] contains the trademark/trade name [2]. Where a trademark or trade name is used in a claim as a limitation to identify or describe a particular material or product, the claim does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(b). The claim scope is uncertain since the trademark/trade name identifies a source, not the goods themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 2 insert the trademark and its position in the claim; in bracket 3 specify the material/product identified by the trademark. See Ex parte Simpson. Reject where trademark/trade name renders identification/description indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Statutory Basis — 35 U.S.C.112(d) (pre-AIA 112, 4th paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotations of 35 U.S.C. 112(d)/pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, fourth paragraph: a claim in dependent form shall contain a reference to a claim previously set forth and then specify a further limitation of the subject matter claimed; a dependent claim shall be construed to incorporate by reference all limitations of the claim to which it refers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.36 must be preceded by 7.30.02 and 7.34.01. Use paragraph 7.36 only once in a given Office action. The statute is required in first actions on merits and final rejections; otherwise use paragraph 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Dependent Claim (35 U.S.C.112(d)/pre-AIA 112, 4th para)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as being of improper dependent form for failing to further limit the subject matter of the claim upon which it depends, or for failing to include all the limitations of the claim upon which it depends. [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may cancel, amend to proper dependent form, rewrite in independent form, or present sufficient showing that the dependent claim complies. In bracket 2 insert explanation of what is in the claim and why it does not constitute a further limitation. Note Federal Circuit holdings that failure to comply renders dependent claim unpatentable; treat as unpatentable (not merely object to form). Must be preceded by 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arguments Are Not Persuasive (general) — 7.37
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's arguments filed [1] have been fully considered but they are not persuasive. [2]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must address all arguments not already responded to in the statement of rejection. In bracket 2 provide explanation as to non-persuasiveness. This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Age of Reference(s) (7.37.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to applicant's argument regarding age of references, the examiner acknowledges obviousness may be shown by combining or modifying teachings of prior art if there is teaching/suggestion/motivation found in the references or in general knowledge available to one of ordinary skill. In this case, [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 explain where the teaching/suggestion/motivation for the rejection is found (references or general knowledge). This form paragraph must be preceded by 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Bodily Incorporation (7.37.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to applicant's argument that [1], the test for obviousness is not whether features of a secondary reference may be bodily incorporated into the structure of the primary reference; rather the test is what the combined teachings of the references would have suggested to those of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 briefly restate applicant's bodily incorporation argument. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Hindsight Reasoning (7.37.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to applicant's argument that the examiner's conclusion of obviousness is based upon improper hindsight reasoning, recognize that any judgment on obviousness is a reconstruction based on hindsight reasoning; it is proper so long as it takes into account only knowledge within the level of ordinary skill at the time and does not include knowledge gleaned only from the applicant's disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.37. In bracketing, refer to applicant's specific arguments. See In re McLaughlin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: No Teaching, Suggestion, or Motivation To Combine (7.37.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to applicant's argument that there is no teaching, suggestion, or motivation to combine the references, the examiner may explain where such teaching/suggestion/motivation is found either in the references themselves or in the knowledge generally available to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific explanation where teaching/suggestion/motivation arises. Use when applicant contends lack of TSM; refer to In re Fine, In re Jones, KSR. Must be preceded by 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Nonanalogous Art (7.37.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: In response to applicant's argument that [1] is nonanalogous art, note that a prior art reference must either be in the field of applicant's endeavor or be reasonably pertinent to the particular problem to be relied upon as a basis for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In bracket 1 enter name of the reference applicant alleges nonanalogous. In bracket 2 explain why the reference is analogous art. Must be preceded by 7.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpersuasive Argument: Number of References (7.37.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Placeholder for examiner response where applicant raises argument concerning the number of references relied upon in an obviousness rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph (and related 7.37 series) to address specific non-persuasive applicant arguments regarding multiple references; must be preceded by 7.37. (Text truncated in chunk; use MPEP for full wording.)
